title: Beef Stroganoff
subtitle: Russian beef fillet in soured cream and mushroom sauce
excerpt: Thin strips of beef fillet, quickly seared, then simmered briefly in a sauce of mushrooms, onion, mustard, and soured cream. A Russian classic that takes under 30 minutes from start to finish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef stroganoff is named after Count Pavel Alexandrovich Stroganov, a 19th-century Russian diplomat, and was codified in Russian cookbooks from around 1870 onwards. The dish was adopted internationally through French cookery books and then widely through 20th-century cookbooks, particularly in Britain and America where it became a popular dinner-party dish. The Russian original is a relatively elegant dish of good-quality beef quickly seared and served in a light soured cream sauce; later versions became richer and heavier with the addition of double cream, paprika, and other ingredients. The key technique is to sear the beef over very high heat for a short time and add it to the sauce only at the very end to avoid overcooking.

recipeTools.notes: Wide and heavy for a fast sear.

content.text: The beef goes in last and stays in the sauce for no more than 1 to 2 minutes: the sear does the cooking, and further time in the sauce makes it tough. The pan must be very hot before the beef goes in and completely uncrowded: cook in small batches if necessary. Do not let the soured cream boil once it is in the sauce; boiling causes it to split and curdle.

items.preparation: cut across the grain into strips 5 mm x 5 cm
tagliatelle or egg noodles, to serve

content.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over the highest heat. Season the beef strips. Sear in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes, tossing, until browned on all sides. Remove from the pan and set aside on a warm plate. Do not wash the pan.

Reduce the heat to medium. Melt the butter in the same pan. Cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook for 6 to 7 minutes until golden and any liquid has evaporated. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the Dijon mustard and stir through.
Add the stock and stir, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce the heat to very low. Add the soured cream and stir until smooth. Do not let the sauce boil. Season with salt and pepper.
Return the seared beef and any resting juices to the sauce. Stir and heat gently for 1 to 2 minutes. Serve immediately over egg noodles or tagliatelle, scattered with parsley.
